name: Persona (ONYX government platform)
description: US identity-verification company (already tracked for its core consumer product) whose separate FedRAMP-authorized government platform, ONYX, offers federal agencies facial recognition, watchlist screening, and Suspicious Activity Report filing capabilities.
notes: Distinct entry from the main 'Persona' company record to specifically document the government/ONYX platform source-code exposure, which is a separate product line from Persona's mainstream consumer identity-verification business used by Discord, OpenAI/ChatGPT, and others.

name: Total Wireless (Verizon)
description: US prepaid wireless carrier owned by Verizon that used identity-verification vendor Veriff to verify customer identity documents for a promotional offer.
notes: Not a dedicated identity-verification vendor; included because its customers' identity documents, submitted via its vendor Veriff, were exposed in a breach of Veriff's systems.

name: Police National Legal Database (PNLD)
description: UK legal-lookup and reference service relied upon by police forces and criminal justice agencies across the UK, holding identity and contact information for police officers, staff, and criminal-justice professionals.
notes: Not a dedicated identity-verification vendor; included because it directly stored and exposed the identity and contact information of police officers, staff, and criminal-justice professionals.

name: FranceConnect+
description: France's official digital-identity single sign-on system, allowing citizens to authenticate to public and private online services using their electronic identity card or other qualified means.
notes: No confirmed public breach identified as of research date; distinct from the separate France Titres (ANTS) breach, which affected the underlying identity-document database rather than the FranceConnect+ authentication layer.

name: SPID (Sistema Pubblico di Identità Digitale, Italy)
description: Italy's public digital-identity system used by over 30 million citizens to access public and private online services with a single set of credentials.
notes: No confirmed public breach identified as of research date.

name: DNIe / Cl@ve (Spain)
description: Spain's national electronic identity card (DNIe) and associated Cl@ve digital-identity authentication system, widely used across public and private sector services.
notes: No confirmed public breach identified as of research date.

name: eID-Funktion / Personalausweis (Germany)
description: Germany's electronic identity function embedded in the national ID card (Personalausweis), enabling online authentication to government and private services via smartphone or card reader.
notes: No confirmed public breach identified as of research date.
